display: A textile artist and natural dyer in Mexico City who writes a newsletter on cochineal and mordant chemistry.

signals.text: I'm looking for buyers for this season's Oaxacan cochineal, ideally before the end of October.
Most buyers want small lots, and shipping and customs abroad are slow, so I need a better way to get cochineal to small brands and dye makers.
This year's harvest is the best I've seen in three years, and I want it to reach people who will pay for that quality.
I'm writing a newsletter issue on why alum-only cochineal goes purple, and on tin versus alum mordants.
Several newsletter readers have asked where to buy true Oaxacan grana, and I don't yet have a good answer for them.
I'm behind on a long funder report for a dye workshop and would welcome help structuring and finishing it.
Local middlemen offer well under what the growers need, so I'm looking for fair-price alternatives.
The dried cochineal is stored in humid conditions, and I'm looking for advice on storing or moving it safely.
I'm trying to understand how to keep cochineal reds from fading, and I'm collecting methods and experiences.
My income depends partly on commission from the cooperative's sales, and I can't predict when it arrives.
I'm stretched between studio work, the cooperative, and the newsletter, and I'd like someone to share the load on sales logistics.

offers.text: Direct access to a cochineal cooperative in the Oaxaca valley, with dried cochineal from the current harvest available.
Small lots of dried Oaxacan cochineal for dye makers and small brands, with a 500 g minimum.
Technical knowledge of mordants (alum, tin, iron, cream of tartar) and how they change cochineal colour.
A dye studio in Coyoacán with eight vats and a loom room, for test batches or colour consulting.
A newsletter with about 2,400 subscribers, mostly textile artists and small brands, where I can feature a relevant project or supplier.
Twelve years of reference swatches from dye tests, which I can use to compare outcomes across mordants and sources.
Photographed side-by-side comparisons of Oaxacan grana and farmed Peruvian cochineal under different mordants.
Workshop teaching on natural dyeing, which I've run for a cultural foundation.

catchers.hypo: I run a small natural-dye shop in Europe. I'd like to buy a few kilos of properly sourced cochineal but can't take a large lot. Can you help?
catchers.can: Sell 500 g or larger lots of ethically sourced Oaxacan cochineal directly from the cooperative, and advise on mordant and shipping.
catchers.confirm: Do you need 500 g or more, ethically sourced, and are you able to handle import paperwork on your side?

catchers.hypo: My dyed reds keep coming out purple or dull, and I use cheap cochineal with alum. What am I doing wrong?
catchers.can: Explain how the choice of cochineal source and mordant affects colour, and suggest a tin and cream of tartar test.
catchers.confirm: Are you dyeing with cochineal on natural fibre and willing to run a small test batch with a different mordant?

catchers.hypo: I'm an importer or distributor of natural dyes, and I'm looking for a reliable supplier in Mexico who can show where the cochineal comes from.
catchers.can: Connect them with the cooperative, with lot sizes, sourcing details and the grower relationship I've built over the years.
catchers.confirm: Can you buy at a fair price that supports the growers, rather than the lowest price available?

catchers.hypo: A friend runs a craft shop abroad and wants a steady source of natural dyes. Do you know anyone who could supply?
catchers.can: Through the textile friend in Barcelona who runs a shop buying natural dyes, I can pass on enquiries or compare notes on small-lot buying.
catchers.confirm: Is the shop interested in natural dyes in small, regular lots rather than a one-off bulk buy?

catchers.hypo: I manage a grant-funded dye or craft project and my final report is overdue. Do you have a way to structure it quickly?
catchers.can: Share how I structure a short funder report, and compare what funders usually want from a workshop report.
catchers.confirm: Is your report mostly about a workshop or craft programme, rather than a technical or financial audit?

catchers.hypo: I'm a textile artist who wants to learn natural dyeing in Mexico City, and I'm looking for a studio with real dye vats.
catchers.can: Host a short studio session or workshop in Coyoacán, or direct them to my newsletter's guides.
catchers.confirm: Are you able to be in Mexico City in person, and are you looking for hands-on dyeing rather than only theory?

catchers.hypo: I'm writing about natural dyes or ethical sourcing and need someone who knows cochineal growers and the market first-hand.
catchers.can: Give an informed interview or introduction to the Oaxaca growers' cooperative, with their consent.
catchers.confirm: Will the piece present the growers fairly and avoid exploiting their story?

catchers.hypo: I run a brand or collective that needs a story and supply chain for naturally dyed textiles. Who could we work with?
catchers.can: Provide cochineal supply, colour development in my studio, and newsletter coverage for a joint collection.
catchers.confirm: Do you plan to use naturally dyed cochineal reds in a real collection within the next few months?

forbids.text: I only sell ethically sourced cochineal, never wild-harvest from protected areas.
I can't travel abroad this autumn, so any collaboration has to work remotely or in Mexico.
I won't sell below a price the growers can live on, even for a quick sale.
I don't share the cooperative's finances or growers' personal details without their agreement.

projects.name: Cochineal cooperative sales
projects.text: Find fair-price buyers for the cooperative's current harvest of dried cochineal, in small and larger lots.

policy.t1: The cooperative's harvest, lot sizes, minimums and the kind of buyer needed, plus my studio and teaching offers.
policy.t2: The cooperative's price pressure and my own commission timing, shared only once a buyer is credible.
policy.never: My personal finances and family details.
